llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate local VMware audit and policy helper, but it needs review because it documents an easy global policy bypass and broad audit exports without enough safety guidance.

dimensions.detail: Local audit logging, rules in ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, agent detection from environment variables, and JSON export are proportionate to an audit/policy skill, but the exported audit data can be operationally sensitive.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via uv package vmware-policy and it may be auto-installed as a dependency of other VMware skills; the artifact contains documentation only, but installation will trust the external package.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime guidance repeatedly documents VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as a way to bypass all policy checks, including in troubleshooting and CLI references, without strong break-glass limits or warnings for production use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists cross-skill audit records under ~/.vmware/audit.db with rotation, and the policy layer defaults to allowing operations when rules are absent or PyYAML is unavailable; this is disclosed but weak for a control layer protecting high-impact VMware operations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: it provides audit logging, policy checks, sanitization, and a decorator used by the VMware skill family, and the artifact says it exposes no MCP tools itself.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing in production. Treat audit exports as sensitive, restrict permissions on ~/.vmware, configure explicit rules, ensure PyYAML is installed, and only allow VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 under documented break-glass procedures with monitoring.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The SKILL.md audit export examples are expected for compliance/audit workflows, but the artifact does not clearly warn that exported audit records may include sensitive operational history.
[SQP-2] expected: The CLI export command is purpose-aligned and includes filters and a limit, but it normalizes writing or piping audit logs without confidentiality guidance.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The CLI reference documents a single environment variable that bypasses policy enforcement across the wrapped VMware tools; that is a material review concern because it is not framed as restricted emergency use.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide also presents the bypass variable as a normal optional environment setting, which under-scopes a high-impact control bypass.
